$comment: D-LK-SQLITE-MACHO-UNDEFINED-LIBSYSTEM-SYMBOLS — the gate-resident RUNTIME witness for all twelve Darwin/libSystem externs that anchor closed: flock/statfs/fstatfs/sysctl/sysctlbyname (unistd.json) + malloc_default_zone/malloc_create_zone/malloc_set_zone_name/malloc_size/malloc_zone_malloc/malloc_zone_free/malloc_zone_realloc (stdlib.json), every one macho-gated. WHY IT EXISTS: with those rows the sqlite testfixture links and runs on arm64 macho, but that sqlite run is NOT in the ctest gate, and the descriptor unit tests (tests/ffi RealUnistdJsonDarwinFsSysctlMachoOnly + RealStdlibJsonMallocZoneMachoOnly, this example's structural twins) pin only the DECLARATIONS — so nothing yet proved these names actually BIND through libSystem and EXECUTE correctly. A wrong signature, a wrong import, or a broken out-param ABI could ship green. This example closes that gap. The macho-only target is DELIBERATE, not an oversight: all twelve rows carry availableObjectFormats [macho], their true owner is libsystem_malloc/libsystem_kernel behind the libSystem umbrella, and there is no elf/pe equivalent — an ungated arm would be a K_SymbolUndefined, so the single arm64-macho target IS the whole honest surface (the macos-latest CI leg; the shipped_strlcpy_strlcat_macho / shipped_bsd_random_futimes_uuid_macho shape). HERMETIC: no ncpu, disk-size, or path-layout assertion — the page size is never compared to a literal, only cross-checked for agreement across sysctl-by-MIB, sysctlbyname and sysconf plus positive-and-power-of-two, so 4 KiB x86_64 and 16 KiB arm64 both pass; the one temp file is /tmp/dss_libsystem_witness_<pid>.tmp, unlink'd immediately after open (the removed name then serves as the guaranteed-nonexistent path for the statfs negative), and every zone block is malloc_zone_free'd. The size_t* out-param is PROVEN not assumed: sysctl gets a 16-byte oldlen over a genuinely 16-byte buffer so the SHRINK is a real write-back, asserted as an invariant (lenMib < sizeof(pgBuf)) rather than the literal 4 — MEASURED, the MIB node reports 4 while sysctlbyname('hw.pagesize') reports 8 when offered room, so a hardcoded 4 would be a latent OS-version flake; both data buffers are pre-poisoned to -1 so a call that writes nothing trips a guard. Exit 42 = (lenMib < sizeof(pgBuf)) 1 + (pgMib - pgName) 0 + (pgConf - pgName) 0 + malloc_size(NULL) 0 + four success rcs 0 + lock/unlock rcs 0 - three exact -1s (+3) + 38 — every operand an opaque extern return, and the out-param shrink, both page-size deltas, szNull and the exact -1 value of the three failure returns are asserted ONLY here (their guards prove nonzero, never the value), so no pass can fold the sum to a literal. malloc_set_zone_name and malloc_zone_free return void and are honestly witnessed by post-conditions (both zones must still allocate after a name change / a free) rather than by a faked result. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete any of the twelve rows → S0001 undeclared identifier at its call, no binary (the descriptors shadow the real SDK headers totally); break any semantic and guard exit codes 1..31 name the exact call. The release arm re-runs every call under the full optimizer.
